name: base64
one_line: base64 encode or decode data and print to standard output
plain: `base64` converts any data (even binary) into plain text made of letters, digits, + and /, and back. It is an encoding, not encryption: anyone can reverse it with no key.
You meet it everywhere: in HTTP Basic auth headers, tokens (JWT), emails, and challenge hints that end with = or ==
when: Decode a string that looks like base64 (ends with =, only A-Za-z0-9+/).
Encode a file to paste it into a form or message.
Decode the parts of a JWT or a Basic auth header.

examples.title: Encode text
examples.explain: -n on echo stops it adding a newline, which would change the result.

examples.title: Decode  (-d)
examples.explain: -d decodes. If the output is binary, redirect it to a file instead of the terminal.

examples.title: Decode a file
examples.explain: Writes the decoded bytes into out.bin. Then check what it is with file out.bin.

examples.title: No line wrapping  (-w 0)
examples.explain: By default lines are wrapped at 76 characters. -w 0 puts everything on one line, as you need for tokens and headers.

examples.title: Ignore junk characters  (-i)
examples.explain: -i skips characters that are not in the base64 alphabet, which helps with pasted text that has stray symbols.

examples.title: Basic auth header
examples.explain: The part after 'Authorization: Basic ' is user:password in base64, so anyone who sees the request can read it.

options.plain: Decode data instead of encoding it.
When decoding, ignore characters that are not part of the base64 alphabet.
options.use: Pasted text with spaces or symbols.

options.plain: Wrap encoded lines after COLS characters (default 76); 0 disables wrapping.

mistakes: Treating base64 as secrecy: it is only a format.
Missing = padding makes decoding fail: add = until the length is a multiple of 4.
URL-safe base64 uses - and _ instead of + and /: translate them first (tr '_-' '/+').
echo adds a newline: use echo -n or printf.
try: Encode your name, then decode it.
Decode a JWT's middle part (add padding if needed).
Decode a base64 file and identify the result with file.
see_also: xxd(1), openssl base64, python3 base64 module, CyberChef (From Base64), basenc(1) for other bases.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
